verdict.rationale: Render documents Git-connected push-to-deploy and Docker support. A community user confirms strong Docker support and Elixir running out of the box, and editor-side work is supported through the official MCP server for Cursor, Claude Code and Codex. However, nothing documents integration with existing external CI pipelines, and broad framework coverage rests on Docker plus one community mention. Missing for 10: documented integration with existing CI systems, explicit evidence of broad framework support without Render-specific config (render.yaml Blueprints are Render's own format), and independent corroboration of Git workflow portability.

support.subject: As a developer, I can keep using my existing Git, CI, editor, and framework workflows without adopting proprietary tooling

citations.quote: Connect your repo and ship with every push.
In addition to great docker support and free static sites, they support distributed Elixir out of the box as well as autoscaling.

Render's Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enables you to manage your Render infrastructure directly from compatible AI apps, such as Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex Desktop, Codex CLI, and Cursor
